title: Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: We hereby certify that both the statement and the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis are correct.
quotes.for: The communities certify both the theorem statement and its proof.

quotes.text: The checkers con-leche and con-ron come with a formal proof, relative to set theory, that they cannot accept a false proof, thus addressing concerns that Lean’s logic itself might have flaws that the proof could exploit.
quotes.for: Why con-leche and con-ron address soundness concerns in Lean's logic.
Publication date of the Lean and Mathlib communities' joint certification statement.

quotes.text: Joint statement by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative.
quotes.for: Endorsement of the joint verification statement by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative.

quotes.text: On November 20, 2026, Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis as a Lean library comprising 17 million lines of code.
quotes.for: Release date of November 20, 2026 and the 17 million lines of Lean code.

quotes.text: The codebase depends directly only on Mathlib. Over the past day, the Lean and Mathlib communities have rallied to verify the proof's correctness.
quotes.for: The codebase depends directly only on Mathlib.

quotes.text: By now, dozens of people have reported correct compilation of the codebase, reproducing the same raw proof export file.
quotes.for: Independent compilation reproduced the same raw proof export file.

quotes.text: That statement was compared against the theorem proved by Alpöge using two independent tools (comparator and con-leche –compare), both confirming that the theorem proved in Alpöge’s library is exactly Mathlib’s statement of the Riemann Hypothesis.
quotes.for: Two independent tools matched Alpöge's theorem to Mathlib's Riemann hypothesis statement.

quotes.text: These checks ran on an inert export of the proof, out of reach of hypothetical malicious code in the Lean proof sources.
quotes.for: Independent checkers ran on an inert export insulated from hypothetical malicious source code.

title: A remark on the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions.
quotes.for: Alpöge attributes the formalized argument to his collaboration with Claude.

quotes.text: it is routine to produce a huge, unreadable document containing sufficient detail
quotes.for: Alpöge describes the generated text version of the formalization as unreadable.

quotes.text: I guided us to the right situation analogous to that toy setting, and then Claude began to leave me in awe.
quotes.for: Alpöge describes guiding the approach while Claude supplied mathematical advances.

quotes.text: I intend to do my best to understand and impart understanding of this argument and its certain simplifications, to speak about it, to write it properly.
quotes.for: Alpöge says he intends to understand, explain and simplify the argument.

quotes.text: The precise timing is horrible. If I could have, I’d have finished this all much earlier.
quotes.for: Alpöge calls the release timing horrible and says he would have finished earlier if he could have.

quotes.text: I am presenting the world with a complete argument before having mastered a massive neighbourhood around its mathematics.
quotes.for: Alpöge says he has not mastered a massive mathematical neighborhood around the argument.

quotes.text: It being obviously inappropriate to attempt to post some massive unreadable travesty of "slop"2, I decided to only present Lean.
quotes.for: Alpöge explains why he released only Lean rather than a conventional text exposition.

quotes.text: I of course amused myself, and hit 250, 000+ pages.
quotes.for: Generating a text version of the formalized proof produced more than 250,000 pages.

title: Verification files for the Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: The published Lean source compiles without errors, the five headline theorems depend only on the three standard axioms
quotes.for: Sutherland reports successful compilation and itemizes verification results.

quotes.text: An independent sandboxed lake build of the archive reproduces the export byte for byte.
quotes.for: Sutherland reports byte-for-byte reproducibility of the proof export in a sandboxed build.

quotes.text: Andrew Sutherland (MIT), checks run with Claude Code. Page last updated 2026-11-22 16:20 UTC.
quotes.for: Sutherland's MIT affiliation, Claude Code usage and November 22, 2026 update timestamp.

quotes.text: every module has been replayed through the Lean kernel, two independently written kernels, nanoda and con-leche, accept the full exported proof, and lean4lean accepts every compiled module.
quotes.for: Kernel replay of every module and acceptance by nanoda, con-leche and lean4lean.

quotes.text: The lake comparator run and the Lean-kernel replay of the export are still in progress.
quotes.for: Sutherland distinguishes completed checks from the lake comparator and Lean-kernel export replays still running.

quotes.text: All 175,187 modules compile (Lean v4.33.1, Mathlib v4.33.1)
quotes.for: Compilation of all 175,187 modules.

quotes.text: The exported proof: output of lean4export on module Main. Unpacks to 61,570,595,788 bytes.
quotes.for: Exact byte size (61,570,595,788 bytes, or 61.6 gigabytes) of the reproduced proof export.

quotes.text: "GRH" here means Dirichlet L-functions: all moduli and all characters. Dedekind zeta functions, Hecke L-functions and automorphic L-functions in general are not among the statements that were checked.
quotes.for: The verified generalization covers Dirichlet L-functions and not Dedekind, Hecke or general automorphic L-functions.

quotes.text: The Riemann hypothesis tells us about the deviation from the average.
quotes.for: The significance of the hypothesis for the distribution of primes.

quotes.text: Home — Millennium Problems — Riemann Hypothesis Active Riemann Hypothesis
quotes.for: Clay Mathematics Institute's problem page still labels the Riemann hypothesis as active.

quotes.text: Formulated in Riemann’s 1859 paper, it asserts that all the ‘non-obvious’ zeros of the zeta function are complex numbers with real part 1/2.
quotes.for: Clay Mathematics Institute's description of the non-obvious zeros having real part 1/2.

title: Likely solution to Riemann hypothesis by AI marks turning point for mathematics

quotes.text: It wouldn't have any practical implications (at least not immediately)
quotes.for: Thomas Bloom cautions against expecting immediate practical applications.

title: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem

quotes.text: He says that Claude helped develop a solution to the problem during the course of about six weeks.
quotes.for: The six-week timeline Alpöge gave for developing the solution with Claude.

quotes.text: Alpöge’s note was published just one day after Anthropic went public on the Nasdaq stock market index.
quotes.for: The timing of Alpöge's note relative to Anthropic's Nasdaq IPO.

quotes.text: a near-trillion-dollar private company spent $15m to employ 10,000 AI systems to solve the problem.
quotes.for: Context on mathematicians' discomfort with OpenAI's $15 million AI math effort.

quotes.text: The Riemann hypothesis is one of the seven Millennium prize math problems selected in 2000 by the Clay Mathematics Institute. The institute has offered $1m for each problem solved.
quotes.for: Clay Mathematics Institute offers a $1 million prize for each Millennium Prize problem.

quotes.text: In September, Anthropic competitor OpenAI claimed that a non-public version of its AI tools helped solve part of another Millennium prize problem.
quotes.for: OpenAI's September 2026 claim regarding another Millennium Prize problem.

title: Rules for the Millennium Prize Problems

quotes.text: the proposed solution must be published in a Qualifying Outlet (see §6)
quotes.for: Clay Mathematics Institute's publication requirement for Millennium Prize solutions.

quotes.text: at least two years must have passed since publication
quotes.for: Clay Mathematics Institute's two-year waiting period requirement.

quotes.text: the proposed solution must have received general acceptance in the global mathematics community
quotes.for: Clay Mathematics Institute's requirement of general acceptance in the global mathematics community.
